public_rationale: Research available before the post documents significant weaknesses in 3D recognition under common corruptions and a remaining object-identification bottleneck in spatial scene question answering. These are substantive limitations in both named areas. The studies also show progress, which is compatible with Marcus's claim that the problems remained challenging and unsolved.
limitations: The studies cover particular tasks rather than every form of perception or scene understanding.
ScanQA combines perception and language; its limitations cannot all be attributed to perception alone.
The ScanQA work first appeared in 2021; the cited evidence is its publicly available May 2022 revision.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that substantial technical failures remained in reliable 3D perception and scene understanding.

criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations document material remaining limitations in both 3D perception and scene understanding.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence establishes broadly reliable solutions in both areas, with remaining errors too limited to sustain the ordinary claim.

evidence.explanation: Testing fifteen common corruptions exposed substantial robustness weaknesses in leading 3D recognition models. The authors also report mitigation methods, so the result establishes remaining challenges rather than an absence of progress.

evidence.locator: Section 5.2, comparison of ScanQA with image-based question-answering baselines
evidence.explanation: The May revision reports that supplying correct object identification can make an image-based baseline competitive with or better than ScanQA. Its authors identify that assistance as unavailable in real-world use, demonstrating a remaining scene-understanding bottleneck.
